title: Winter Hiking Guide & Cold Weather Checklist, Printable PDF, What to Wear by Temperature, Beginner Hiker Gift, Snow Hike Planner
description:
Keep hiking after the first frost. A 22-page printable guide for beginner and intermediate hikers on winter day hikes: how to layer, how to plan around short daylight, when you need microspikes, and the cold-weather warning signs, in plain words.

WHAT'S INSIDE
- How winter hiking is different, and how to pick a winter trail and a turnaround time
- Layering explained: base, mid and shell, and why to skip cotton
- Hands, feet, head and neck
- Traction: boots, microspikes and snowshoes, and when to turn back
- Water, food, batteries and phones in the cold; sun and snow glare
- Cold-weather warning signs (frostnip, frostbite, hypothermia basics) and when to get help
- Avalanche awareness with links to official sources (NPS, avalanche.org, Avalanche Canada)
- Printable winter day-hike checklist and a layering checklist by temperature in °F and °C
- Trip plan to leave with someone, winter car kit, a cut-out quick-check card and hike log pages

WHAT YOU GET
- US Letter and A4 versions
- Color and printer-friendly (low ink) versions
- Instant download. This is a digital file; nothing is shipped.
- Bonus: our free one-page Ultimate Hiking Checklist

GOOD TO KNOW
This is general safety information for day hikes, not medical advice and not avalanche training. Always check local conditions and park rangers before you go.

Made by HikeSupply Co., a small shop for weekend hikers. More printable guides at hikesupplyco.com
